chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Do not anoint yourself with oil containing musk or amber when you intend to enter the state of Ihram, because its scent remains in your head after you have entered Ihram. And anoint yourself with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter Ihram; but once you have entered Ihram, the oil becomes forbidden for you until you exit Ihram."

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تُحِلّ: To exit the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using scented oil before and during Hajj Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies a practical nuance in the jurisprudence of Ihram: while the application of oil itself becomes prohibited upon entering the state, the lingering scent of musk or ambergris applied beforehand remains permissible because the prohibition targets the oil's presence, not its residual aroma. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific intent and physical state of the prohibited item, ensuring pilgrims can maintain hygiene and pleasantness without invalidating their ritual status.
